brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: A 2×2 stack of half bases, dressed with workshop tools (props 1–5).
The half bases sit on level 0 (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) and level 1 (piece:0,0,1 and piece:1,0,1).
bin:0,0,1 (split 3 ways) and bin:1,0,1 (split 2 ways) on level 1.
drawer:0#0,0#cut on the cut face of the level-0 half base piece:0,0,0.

Every other open edge has a solid cap, and joints are bolted with lockJoints. One edge (1,0,0;*;150) is open: its cap hits the drawer frame (MESH_CLASH), the configurator offers no other part for it, and check_build lists it as OPEN_CAP_FACE.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey organizer from two columns of north-half hex bases. The top storey has two bins and the bottom storey has one drawer. One edge is still uncapped: the end cap for that spot hits the drawer frame (MESH_CLASH), so I left it open. Joints are bolted. check_build reports no rule errors and meshClash "clear". I dressed it with a brush, a marker, a pencil and a pen standing in the bins and electrical tape in the drawer. The screwdriver, file, hex driver and hex key set would not stay standing in the 3-way bin, and nothing would lie in the drawer, so I left them out.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
